2022session 2
2022 · 2nd session · Exercise 1 · 7 pts · official key

Effect of the launching speed on the amplitude

Diff. eq.T₀, ω₀EnergyGraphs

A mechanical oscillator consists of a block (S) of mass m and a spring of negligible mass and force constant k=20 N/m. The spring is connected from one of its ends to a fixed support A; (S) is attached to the other end and may slide without friction on a horizontal support (Doc. 1). At equilibrium, G, the center of mass of (S), coincides with the origin O of the x-axis.

At the instant t0​=0, G is at O and we launch (S) with a velocity v0​=v0​i; thus (S) undergoes mechanical oscillations of amplitude Xm​. At an instant t, the abscissa of G is x=OG and the algebraic value of its velocity is v=x′=dtdx​.

The aim of this exercise is to study the effect of v0​ on the amplitude Xm​. Take: the horizontal plane through G as reference level for gravitational potential energy; g=10 m/s2 and π2=10.

1) Theoretical study

  1. 1.1Write the expression of the mechanical energy ME of the system (Oscillator, Earth) in terms of x, m, k and v.
  2. 1.2Determine the second order differential equation that governs the variation of x.
  3. 1.3Deduce the expression of the proper (natural) period T0​ of the oscillations in terms of m and k.

2) Experimental study

An appropriate device gives the elastic potential energy EPE of the oscillator as a function of time for two different experiments (Doc. 2).

  1. 2.1.1Use document 2 to justify that the oscillations of (S) are undamped.
  2. 2.1.2Copy and complete the table: maximum value of EPE and period TE​ of EPE, for experiments 1 and 2.
  3. 2.2Show that m=0.5 kg knowing that T0​=2TE​.
  4. 2.3Show that Xm(2)​=2Xm(1)​.
  5. 2.4Determine the values of v0​ for the two experiments.
  6. 2.5Deduce whether Xm​ increases, decreases, or remains the same as v0​ increases.

2022 · 1st session · Exercise 2 · 7 pts · official key

Finding the mass and the time equation

EnergyT₀, ω₀Time eq.Graphs

A mechanical oscillator is formed of a block (S) of mass m and a horizontal light spring of force constant k=100 N/m, connected from one end to a fixed support A; (S) is attached to the other end and slides without friction on a horizontal surface. At equilibrium, G coincides with the origin O of the x-axis.

At t0​=0, G is at O and (S) is launched in the negative direction with an initial velocity V0​. At an instant t, the abscissa of G is x=OG and the algebraic value of its velocity is v=x′=dtdx​.

The curve of document 3 represents, as a function of time, one of these three forms of energy: the kinetic energy, the elastic potential energy, or the mechanical energy of the system (Oscillator, Earth). The horizontal plane containing G is taken as the reference level for gravitational potential energy.

  1. 1Specify the type of the oscillations of G.
  2. 2The curve of document 3 represents the elastic potential energy of the system. Why?
  3. 3.1Using document 3, calculate the amplitude Xm​.
  4. 3.2Knowing that the period of EPE is Tenergy​=2T0​​, calculate T0​.
  5. 4.1The time equation is x=Xm​sin(ω0​t+φ). Determine the value of φ.
  6. 4.2Calculate the value of ω0​.
  7. 4.3Deduce the expression of x as a function of time.
  8. 5Knowing that ω0​=k/m​, calculate the value of m.
2021session 2
2021 · 2nd session · Exercise 1 · 7 pts · official key

Maximum speed of an oscillator

Diff. eq.T₀, ω₀EnergyGraphs

A mechanical oscillator consists of a block (S) of mass m=50 g and a massless spring of force constant k. The horizontal spring is fixed from one end to a support A; (S) is attached to the other end and moves without friction on a horizontal surface. At equilibrium, G coincides with the origin O of the x-axis.

(S) is shifted from its equilibrium position by a displacement x0​ and released without initial velocity at t0​=0. At an instant t, the abscissa of G is x=OG and the algebraic value of its velocity is v=x′=dtdx​.

The aim is to determine the maximum speed attained by G. Take: the horizontal plane containing G as reference for gravitational potential energy; π2=10.

  1. 1The mechanical energy ME of the system (Oscillator, Earth) is conserved. Why?
  2. 2Write the expression of ME in terms of m, v, k and x.
  3. 3Determine the second order differential equation in x that governs the motion of G.
  4. 4Deduce, in terms of m and k, the expression of the proper period T0​.
  5. 5.1An appropriate device shows x as a function of time (Doc. 2).Indicate the values of T0​ and x0​.
  6. 5.2Deduce the value of k.
  7. 5.3Prove that ME=6.25×10−2 J.
  8. 5.4Using document 2, indicate an instant at which the elastic potential energy is zero.
  9. 5.5Determine the maximum speed attained by G.

  3. 3Deduce that T1​=2πkM​​.

2018 · 2nd session · Exercise 1 · 7 pts · official key

Stiffness of a spring after a collision

+ CollisionDiff. eq.Time eq.T₀, ω₀

To determine the stiffness k of a spring (R), we consider: a track CEOD in a vertical plane, formed of a curved part CE and a horizontal part EOD; a horizontal spring (R) of negligible mass; two identical objects (S₁) and (S₂), considered as particles, of the same mass m. (R) is fixed at B; its other end is connected to (S₂). At equilibrium, (S₂) is at the origin O of a horizontal x-axis of unit vector i.

(S₁) is released without initial speed from C, at height hC​=5 cm above the x-axis. Neglect all friction. Take: the horizontal plane containing the x-axis as reference for gravitational potential energy; g=10 m/s2; π=3.14.

  1. 1(S₁) reaches (S₂) with velocity V1​=V1​i. Apply conservation of the mechanical energy of [(S₁), Earth] to determine V1​.
  2. 2(S₁) enters a head-on elastic collision with (S₂), initially at rest. Verify that just after the collision (S₁) is at rest and (S₂) moves with V0​=1 m/s.
  3. 3.1After the collision (S₂) oscillates; t0​=0 is the instant of the collision at O. Establish the differential equation in x.
  4. 3.2The solution is x=Asin(T0​2π​t). 3.2.1) Determine T0​ in terms of m and k. 3.2.2) Determine A in terms of V0​ and T0​. 3.2.3) Name the characteristic A.
  5. 4At t1​=314 ms, (S₂) returns to O for the first time. Deduce T0​.
  6. 5Calculate A.
  7. 6Determine by two different methods the value of k, knowing that m=400 g.
2017session 2
2017 · 2nd session · Exercise 3 · 7 pts · official key

Mass of a block and stiffness of a spring

+ CollisionEnergyGraphsFind k, m

Consider two blocks, (A) of unknown mass mA​ and (B) of mass mB​=0.8 kg, and a spring (R) of negligible mass and stiffness k. The aim is to determine mA​ and k. Neglect all friction; take g=10 m/s2.

1) First experiment: determination of mA​

The spring is compressed between (A) and (B) by a light string on a horizontal track (Doc. 1). The centers of mass of (A) and (B) are in the same horizontal plane, taken as reference for gravitational potential energy. The x-axis is positive to the right. We burn the string; (A) and (B) are ejected in opposite directions.

  1. 1.1Name the external forces acting on the system [(A), (B), (R)].
  2. 1.2Deduce that the linear momentum of the system is conserved on the horizontal track.
  3. 1.3Just after ejection, VB​=0.75i (m/s). 1.3.1) Determine the linear momentum PA​ of (A). 1.3.2) Deduce VA​ in terms of mA​.
  4. 1.4(A) reaches the curved path CD; the maximum height of its center of mass is hmax​=5 cm. 1.4.1) Use conservation of ME of [(A), Earth] to determine VA​. 1.4.2) Deduce mA​.

2) Second experiment: determination of k

Block (B) is fixed to one end of (R), the other end attached to a fixed support. At equilibrium, (B) is at O. (B) is displaced from O by a distance Xm​ in the negative direction and released without initial velocity at t0​=0. Between t0​=0 and t=T0​/2, a system traces the speed of G as a function of time (Doc. 3) and as a function of the abscissa x (Doc. 4).

  1. 2.1Determine, using document 3, the maximum kinetic energy of (B).
  2. 2.2Deduce the maximum elastic potential energy of the system [(R), (B), Earth].
  3. 2.3Indicate, using document 4, the value of Xm​.
  4. 2.4Deduce the value of k.

Two methods to find the stiffness

At t0​=0, G is at rest at O and (S) is launched in the positive direction. At an instant t, the abscissa of G is x=OG and the algebraic value of its velocity is v=x′=dtdx​. The horizontal plane through G is the reference for gravitational potential energy. Take π2=10.

1) First method

An apparatus traces x as a function of time (Doc. 2).

  1. 1.1Referring to document 2, indicate: 1.1.1) the type of the oscillations (justify); 1.1.2) the amplitude Xm​; 1.1.3) the proper period T0​.
  2. 1.2Indicate the nature of the motion of G and choose the differential equation: (1) x′+mk​x=0; (2) x′′+mk​x=0; (3) x′′+mk​x′=0.

Harmonic oscillator and its energies

Diff. eq.T₀, ω₀Time eq.EnergyGraphs

A small trolley (C) of mass m=200 g is attached to one extremity of a horizontal spring (R) of negligible mass, of un-jointed loops and stiffness k=20 N/m; the other extremity is attached to a fixed support. (C) slides without friction on a horizontal rail; G moves along x′Ox.

At t0​=0, G is at its equilibrium position O and (C) is launched with V0​=−V0​i (V0​>0); (C) then oscillates with proper angular frequency ω0​. At an instant t, the abscissa of G is x=OG and the algebraic value of its velocity is v=x′=dtdx​. The horizontal plane containing G is taken as the reference level for gravitational potential energy.

A — Theoretical study

  1. A.1Write the expression of ME of the system [(C), (R), Earth] in terms of m, k, x and v.
  2. A.2Derive the differential equation in x.
  3. A.3The solution is x=−Xm​sin(ω0​t) (Xm​>0). a) Determine ω0​ in terms of k and m. b) Deduce T0​.
  4. A.4Determine Xm​ in terms of V0​, k and m.

B — Energetic study

A device gives the kinetic energy, the elastic potential energy and the mechanical energy of the system as functions of time (Fig. 2).

  1. B.1Indicate, with justification, the energy corresponding to each curve.
  2. B.2Curves (2) and (3) are periodic of period T. a) Pick up T. b) Deduce the relation between T and T0​.
  3. B.3Write the expression of E0​ in terms of m and V0​.
  4. B.4Deduce the value of V0​.

(S) is pulled vertically downwards and released without initial velocity at t0​=0; G oscillates about O. At an instant t, G is defined by x=OG (axis directed downwards) and v=dtdx​. The horizontal plane through O is the reference for gravitational potential energy.

From a pendulum to a spring oscillator

+ CollisionEnergyDiff. eq.Time eq.

A pendulum is formed of a massless inextensible string of length ℓ=1.8 m, one end C fixed, the other carrying a particle (P₁) of mass m1​=200 g. The string is stretched horizontally and (P₁), at A₀, is launched vertically downward with a speed Vi​=8 m/s. At the lowest position A, (P₁) collides head-on and perfectly elastically with a particle (P₂) of mass m2​=300 g initially at rest. Neglect all friction.

Take the horizontal plane through A as reference for gravitational potential energy; g=10 m/s2.

A — Collision

  1. 1a) Calculate the mechanical energy of [pendulum, Earth] when (P₁) is launched at A₀. b) Determine the speed V1​ of (P₁) just before the collision.
  2. 2a) Name the quantities conserved during the collision. b) Show that the speed of (P₂) just after the collision is V2′​=8 m/s.

B — Mechanical oscillator

A horizontal spring (S) of stiffness K=120 N/m is fixed at B; its other end carries a ring R. (P₂) moves on AB, hits R at O and sticks to it, forming a particle (P) of mass m=1.2 kg that oscillates without friction along x′Ox. Just after this, at t0​=0, G is at O (equilibrium) with V0​=V0​i, V0​=2 m/s. At an instant t, the abscissa of G is x=OG and the algebraic value of its velocity is v=x′=dtdx​.

  1. B.1Write ME of the system (oscillator, Earth) in terms of K, m, x and v.
  2. B.2Derive the differential equation and deduce the nature of the motion.
  3. B.3The solution is x=Xm​cos(mK​​t+φ). Determine Xm​ and φ.

Free, damped and driven oscillations

EnergyDiff. eq.Time eq.Damping

A horizontal elastic pendulum is formed of a puck (A) of mass m=200 g and a spring of un-jointed turns, of negligible mass and stiffness k=80 N/m. G is located on x′x by x=OG; its velocity is V=Vi with V=x′. The horizontal plane containing G is the reference for gravitational potential energy.

A — Free undamped oscillations

At t0​=0, G is at O and (A) is launched with V0​=V0​i (V0​=2.5 m/s); (A) moves without friction.

  1. 1Calculate ME of the system [(A), spring, Earth].
  2. 2a) Give ME at instant t in terms of x, k, m and V. b) Determine the differential equation. c) Determine ω0​ and T0​.
  3. 3The solution is x=Xm​cos(ω0​t+φ). Determine Xm​ and φ.

B — Damped oscillations; driving the oscillations

G is at rest at O. (A) is shifted by 12.5 cm and released from rest at t0​=0; it performs pseudo-periodic oscillations of pseudo-period T. After 10 oscillations the amplitude is 12 cm.

  1. 1Calculate the variation of ME during these 10 oscillations.

A spring of un-jointed loops, stiffness k=10 N/m and horizontal axis, is fixed at one end; the other end carries a puck M of mass m=100 g. G slides without friction along x′x (origin O, unit vector i). The horizontal plane through G is the reference for gravitational potential energy.

At t0​=0, M, at rest at O, is hit by a puck M′ of mass m′=2m​ moving with V′=−V′i (V′>0). After the collision, M′ rebounds with V1′​ and M moves with V0​=V0​i, then oscillates with constant amplitude Xm​=10 cm.

The aim is to determine the stiffness k of the spring of a horizontal oscillator formed of a solid (S₁) of mass M=400 g and a spring of negligible mass. G moves on x′Ox; O is its equilibrium position.

A — Setting the oscillator in motion

(S₁) is at rest, G at O. A solid (S₂) of mass m=2M​ is launched toward (S₁) along x′Ox with velocity V2​=V2​i (V2​=0.75 m/s). The collision is elastic; (S₂) rebounds and (S₁) acquires V0​=V0​i.

  1. 1a) Write PEe​ in terms of k, Xm​, M, t. b) Determine KE. c) Find ME in terms of k and Xm​. d) Deduce that (S₁) is not subjected to friction.
